Q: MS Excel displays garbled characters for Azerbaijani text in CSV file exported with UTF-8 encoding A:

I assume you are not using Java 1 as indicated. It may be that you've simply messed up source file encoding for javac. Test with simple program that writes your expected text:

Files.writeString(Path.of("az.csv"), "\ufeffRiskli vergi ödəyicilərinin axtarışı");

If I compile + run this on JDK14 (javac assumes files are Windows default charset) then the chars are mangled when reading in Excel. If I compile + run with JDK18+ see JEP-400 UTF-8 by default or with JDK14 as javac -Dfile.encoding=UTF-8 then Excel has no issues reading those characters in az.csv.

Q: Nmap running with very trivial script as argument not throwing expected string expected to be triggered depending on TCP port state (open/closed) A:

Nmap uses an internal efficiency system.
In recent versions of nmap, the script engine is so demanding that could choose to silently omit a script if it doesn’t detect a real service. Nmap is obsessed with speed so it will resist by all means to consider any closed port. It may also consider the table as “empty” if it’s made from closed ports.

By default, scripts that rely on portrule, are only executed against ports nmap considers interesting (usually: open, open | filtered/unfiltered) and it can also treat scripts in a different manner in front of certain local network configurations (e.g. localhost/127.0.0.1).
When a port is marked as closed, nmap assumes there is no service listening and to save resources it will not try to execute scripts against it, for example, ignoring portrule although condition was logically correct.

Solution: hostrule and the nmap library:
nmap’s API could be colliding with your system's data structure. Try using nmap’s official library to get the ports.
Key idea is to avoid “free table” or “null value” that would trigger an error.

nmap -p80,443 --script testy2closed_hostrule_lib.nse 127.0.0.1

Starting Nmap 7.98 ( https://nmap.org ) at 2026-02-14 12:33 +0100
Nmap scan report for localhost (127.0.0.1)
Host is up (0.000056s latency).

PORT    STATE  SERVICE
80/tcp  closed http
443/tcp closed https

Host script results:
testy2closed_hostrule_lib: 
Port 80: This port is closed!
|_Port 443: This port is closed!

cat testy2closed_hostrule_lib.nse

local nmap = require "nmap" -- Load the library explicitly

description = [[ Test closed ports ]]
author = "Peter"
categories = {"safe"}

-- Hostrule to asure execution
hostrule = function(host)
  return true
end

action = function(host)
  local result = {}

  -- Specifically looking for TCP ports with CLOSED status
  local port = nmap.get_port_state(host, {number=80, protocol="tcp"})
  if port and port.state == "closed" then
    table.insert(result, "Port 80: This port is closed!")
  end

  port = nmap.get_port_state(host, {number=443, protocol="tcp"})
  if port and port.state == "closed" then
    table.insert(result, "Port 443: This port is closed!")
  end

  if #result > 0 then
    return "\n" .. table.concat(result, "\n")
  end
end

*Your script can be in the working directory. (./name.nse or name.nse). Nmap will look for it there after searching the official directory. If script lives in a different path, you should specify through command-line option (—e.g. --script /home/user/scripts/test.nse).

Alternative attempts (that didn't work, at least for me, but worth knowing):

  • Add a plus sign (+) before the name of the script in the command line. This tells nmap to ignore usual restrictions and execute the script for any scanned port. nmap -p80,443 --script +testy2closed.nse 127.0.0.1 If + didn’t work, probably is due to that specific conditions are still ongoing.

  • Adding intrusive category. Turns nmap to be less protective.

At the beginning of your source code:
categories = {"intrusive"}
Command-line:
nmap -p80,443 --script testy2closed.nse --script-args unsafe=1 127.0.0.1

  • Instead of portrule (that lies on nmap decision to consider a port interesting), use hostrule (first without nmap library). This rule is always executed for the host and from there yo can manually query the state of any port.

  • Try using --reason command-line option. Forcing NSE engine to maintain port in memory to process the scripts.

Q: Discord voice.play(source) doesn't do anything A:

If this source line is literally what is running, then I suspect that line might be the problem:

source = discord.FFmpegPCMAudio(source=source)

It looks like source isn’t defined there. You pulled:

url = info["url"]

but you did not pass it into FFmpeg. So FFmpeg likely starts with a bad/empty input and exits immediately, that’s the “process terminated” log.

You probably want:

audio = discord.FFmpegPCMAudio(url, **FFMPEG_OPTIONS) voice.play(audio)

Q: CodeIgniter query() with directly injected $_POST data in INSERT IGNORE query emits a syntax error A:

Try this : your query was missing single quotes to the string type of value like email, lang and ip

$query = $this->db->query("
   INSERT IGNORE INTO ".$table." (email, lang, ip_address) 
   VALUES ('".$this->db->escape($_POST['email'])."', '".$this->db->escape($lang)."', '".$this->input->ip_address()."')");

Q: How to use FFmpeg to register certain Codecs? A:

Short answer: you can't register a codec standalone (as user).

Long answer: Inspecting avcodec_register_all() found in libavcodec/allcodecs.c we can see how it registers the codecs, hardware accelerators and others.

For example if we would want to register a decoder which has CODEC_ID_H264 we should call avcodec_register(&ff_h264_decoder). The problem is that the ff_h264_decoder is defined only in libavcodec/h264.c but not in any header files thus we can not refer to it.

Then who should use avcodec_register? Users can not, developers should. It is the way of registering a custom avcodec. Good thing is calling avcodec_register_all() more times does not cause problemas, as it registers everything only once.

Q: CodeIgniter's where() method renders a broken query when backticks are manually used on a table alias A:

The problem is your single quotes.

Change this:

$this->db->where('`tgs`.lang_id', $lang_id);

To this:

$this->db->where('tgs.lang_id', $lang_id);

Q: On Gitlab, Is it possible to set a specific Wiki page different than "home"? A:

If you don't have an Page with the "Path" set to "home" you can do the following.

Go to the Page you want as the "Start Page" and rename the path to "home":

Its also important that the checkbox "Generate page path from title" is not set.
Also i needed to edit the Title for the Page again, since it was set to "Home" but after changing it again to "README" (in my case) the Title stayed as is.

Fazit:
* use Path "home" & save
* rename Title again to what you really want, the second time it should keep the title
